div.head: Hn 64.1f
div.ab: Malorum autem infestacionibus et periurancium conspiracione dispositum est frangens iuramentum, ut magis Dei iudicium ab accusatis eligatur.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 584 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)

note.seg: wegen (infolge) der Rotte Meineidiger ist Stabeid [mit Formerschwerung] angeordnet, damit [statt seiner Gefahr] man verklagt lieber Gottesurtheil [zur Reinigung] wähle; vgl. Formul. iudic. Dei ed. Zeumer (Mon. Germ. Leg. V) 619: Iudicium per Eugenium [II] inuentum est, ut nulli liceat iurare

on account of (in consequence of) the band of perjurers the formal oath [with its aggravated form] has been ordained, so that [instead of incurring its danger] the accused may rather choose the judgment of God [for purgation]; cf. Formul. iudic. Dei ed. Zeumer (Mon. Germ. Leg. V) 619: Iudicium per Eugenium [II] inuentum est, ut nulli liceat iurare

infestina. et iur. Rs; vgl. 11, 16a—dep.{5} Rs, als ‘laid aside’ von Stubbs (Lect. 171) angenommen: aber die Mehrzahl der Eide war ungestabt, also sank das Meineidsquantum (wie der Sinn des depositum bedingen würde) nicht durch Abschaffung des Stabeides; s. d. Gl 2

infestina. et iur. Rs; cf. 11, 16a—dep.{5} Rs, taken by Stubbs (Lect. 171) as ‘laid aside’: but the majority of oaths were not formal, so the amount of perjury did not fall (as the sense of depositum would require) through the abolition of the formal oath; see that word in Gl 2
